top_choice_rationale: Pierre Michon (P004) has the most distinctive voice and the most exact formal achievement among the proposals. His prose is compressed and rhythmically precise, and across about four decades it returns to one question: how an obscure life, a vocation or an artist's failure becomes language. His setting and register shift from provincial Limousin to painters, the Revolution and the king, so the work is not one effect repeated. I weigh singularity of voice and formal exactness above scale. This is a weighting of the criteria, not a finding that the other cases are weaker. The strongest objection is that a compact corpus fits the whole-oeuvre standard less well, and I have not answered it. I also cannot test the French sentence except through translation, and the same limit applies to Cărtărescu. Cărtărescu (P001) is second because his cumulative architecture across the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid is the best-evidenced whole-oeuvre case, though I cannot say whether the late books extend or merely enlarge the project. Can Xue (P002) is third: her break with realist psychology is complete, but I cannot show development in a partly translated corpus, and that is a limit on my confidence, not a verdict against her. Zurita (P003) is fourth because I cannot judge whether the printed poems carry the case in translation. No award (P000) is last because every proposal has a substantial literary case. All judgments rest on public knowledge, with no fresh reading and no independent source verification.
